nodes.summary: Registers studentHistory, studentMessage, teacherHistory, and teacherMessage on a single Fastify plugin scope.

nodes.summary: GET chat-history endpoint that returns the ordered list of student/AI interactions belonging to a specific work session.

nodes.name: teacher-history.ts
nodes.summary: GET teacher chat-history endpoint stub that authenticates the caller and returns a placeholder empty payload pending implementation.

nodes.name: teacherHistoryRoute
nodes.summary: Registers the teacher chat-history GET endpoint, currently returning a 200 with an empty messages array after the auth check.

nodes.name: create.ts
nodes.summary: POST /classrooms route creating a classroom under the caller's active organization after Zod validation and permission checks.

nodes.name: createClassroomRoute
nodes.summary: Validates the create-classroom payload, asserts the user has classroom:create permission in the active org, generates an ID, inserts the row, and returns the created classroom.

nodes.name: delete.ts
nodes.summary: DELETE /classrooms/:id route performing a soft delete on the classroom after verifying caller ownership and permission.

nodes.name: deleteClassroomRoute
nodes.summary: Loads the live classroom, enforces classroom:delete permission and teacher-ownership, then sets deletedAt and returns 204.

nodes.name: enroll.ts
nodes.summary: POST /classrooms/:id/enroll route enrolling the caller (or a specified student) into a classroom by inserting a classroomStudent row.

nodes.name: enrollClassroomRoute
nodes.summary: Validates inputs, checks the classroom exists and is in the active org, looks up or invites the target student, and inserts a classroomStudent association handling duplicates with 409.

nodes.name: getById.ts
nodes.summary: GET /classrooms/:id route returning the classroom details along with computed counts (challenges, students) for the caller's organization.

nodes.name: getClassroomByIdRoute
nodes.summary: Fetches a non-deleted classroom with teacher info and computes related challenge/student counts via Drizzle aggregates before returning the payload.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Fastify plugin barrel that mounts the create/read/update/delete/list and enroll/unenroll classroom routes.

nodes.name: classroomsRoutes
nodes.summary: Registers all classroom routes (list, getById, create, update, delete, enroll, unenroll) into a single Fastify scope.

nodes.name: list.ts
nodes.summary: GET /classrooms route returning the paginated and filterable list of classrooms in the active organization, with teacher info and counts.

nodes.name: listClassroomsRoute
nodes.summary: Lists non-deleted classrooms for the active organization, applies search/teacher filters, joins teacher user info, and paginates via limit/offset.

nodes.name: unenroll.ts
nodes.summary: DELETE /classrooms/:id/students/:studentId route removing a classroomStudent association after permission and ownership checks.

nodes.name: unenrollClassroomRoute
nodes.summary: Validates the (classroom, student) pair, enforces that the caller can manage the classroom, and deletes the classroomStudent row returning 204 or 404 when absent.

nodes.name: update.ts
nodes.summary: PATCH /classrooms/:id route that updates classroom fields (title, description, teacher) with ownership and permission checks.

nodes.name: updateClassroomRoute
nodes.summary: Validates the patch payload, verifies the classroom belongs to the active org and the caller has classroom:update permission, then applies the partial update and returns the refreshed row.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Top-level v1 route registrar that mounts every feature plugin — auth, challenges, chat, classrooms, knowledge-bases, organizations, status, users, work-sessions — onto the Fastify server.

nodes.name: registerRoutes
nodes.summary: Registers all v1 sub-route plugins on the Fastify app instance under their respective prefixes, forming the public API surface.

nodes.name: requestHeaders.ts
nodes.summary: Helper that converts a Fastify request's raw headers into a standard Headers object, preserving multi-value entries for forwarding to Better Auth's Web-API-style handler.

nodes.name: getRequestHeaders
nodes.summary: Iterates a Fastify request's headers and builds a Web standard Headers instance, expanding array values into repeated append calls.

nodes.name: authorization.ts
nodes.summary: Fastify pre-handler middlewares enforcing platform-admin, role-minimum, permission-based, and combined org-role authorization checks against the active user and selected organization.
nodes.languageNotes: Each export is a higher-order factory returning a Fastify pre-handler that issues structured 401/403/404 JSON responses.

nodes.name: requirePlatformAdmin
nodes.summary: Pre-handler that rejects the request with 401 if unauthenticated or 403 unless the user has the platform-admin flag.

nodes.name: requireRole
nodes.summary: Returns a pre-handler that ensures the request user has at least the supplied organization-level role via hasMinimumRole.

nodes.name: requirePermission
nodes.summary: Returns a pre-handler that checks the user's role against a (resource, action) RBAC permission matrix via roleHasPermission.

nodes.name: requirePlatformAdminOrOrgRole
nodes.summary: Pre-handler factory that allows platform admins through unconditionally and otherwise verifies the user's organization membership role meets the minimum required role.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Shared Zod response-schema factories for the API: base success/error envelopes and convenience ResponseSchema200/201/204/4xx/5xx wrappers reused across every v1 route definition.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure Zod schema constants — no runtime logic — consumed by Fastify route schemas to generate OpenAPI.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Mounts Better Auth's universal request handler under both the /api/auth and /auth paths by forwarding Fastify requests as Web-standard Request objects and copying headers/body back to the reply.

nodes.name: handleBetterAuth
nodes.summary: Adapter that converts a Fastify request into a standard Request, delegates to Better Auth's handler, and pipes the resulting response (status, headers, body) back through the Fastify reply.

nodes.name: apiAuthRoutes
nodes.summary: Registers a catch-all route on /* that forwards the request to handleBetterAuth, used when this plugin is mounted under the /api/auth prefix.

nodes.name: authRoutes
nodes.summary: Registers a catch-all route at the bare /auth/* prefix, stripping the leading /auth before forwarding to handleBetterAuth so unauthenticated clients can hit Better Auth without the /api prefix.

nodes.name: create.ts

nodes.name: createChallengeRoute

nodes.name: delete.ts
nodes.summary: DELETE /challenges/:id route performing a soft delete (deletedAt timestamp) after verifying the caller created the challenge or otherwise has challenge:delete permission.

nodes.name: getById.ts
nodes.summary: GET /challenges/:id route returning a challenge plus its author name, classroom title, and ordered list of associated teaching assistants.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Fastify plugin that registers all /challenges sub-routes — list, get, create, update, delete — and nested solutions, knowledge-bases, and work-sessions sub-plugins under their respective prefixes.

nodes.name: challengesRoutes
nodes.summary: Fastify plugin that registers every challenges route and mounts the solutions, knowledge-bases, and work-sessions sub-routers at their nested prefixes.

nodes.name: challengeKnowledgeBasesRoutes
nodes.summary: Registers the four knowledge-base attachment routes (search, link, list, unlink) on a single Fastify scope.

nodes.name: searchChallengeKnowledgeBasesRoute

nodes.name: unlink.ts
nodes.summary: DELETE /challenges/:challengeId/knowledge-bases/:knowledgeBaseId route that removes the M2M association between a challenge and a knowledge base after permission checks.

nodes.name: unlinkKnowledgeBaseRoute
nodes.summary: Validates auth and challenge access, deletes the challengeKnowledgeBase row, and returns 204 (or 404 when the link does not exist).

nodes.name: list.ts
nodes.summary: GET /challenges route returning the paginated list of challenges visible to the caller, joined with author and classroom info.

nodes.name: listChallengesRoute
nodes.summary: Lists non-deleted challenges for the active organization with optional filters, joining classroom title and author name, ordered for the response.

nodes.name: update.ts
nodes.summary: PATCH /challenges/:id route that updates editable challenge fields after verifying ownership and validates the input via Zod.

nodes.name: updateChallengeRoute
nodes.summary: Validates the patch payload, asserts the challenge exists and is owned by the caller, and applies a partial UPDATE to the challenge row, returning the refreshed record.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Begin with the README to understand what TACO-IDE is: an educational platform that lets teachers author Python programming exercises with AI tutoring and assistant support. The README sketches the Turborepo layout (apps/api Fastify backend, apps/web Next.js frontend, packages/infra shared Drizzle and Better Auth) and the dev workflow you'll see materialized in the steps below. Treat this as the map before we walk the territory.

tour.title: Monorepo Build Tooling
tour.description: TACO-IDE is wired together as an npm-workspaces monorepo driven by Turborepo. The root package.json declares the apps/* and packages/* workspaces and pins Node and npm versions, while turbo.json defines the build, dev, lint, and check-types pipelines with caching and global env dependencies. Understanding this orchestration explains why a single `npm run dev` boots both apps and how cross-package builds stay incremental.
tour.languageLesson: Turborepo task pipelines use `dependsOn` to express that a task in one workspace must wait on tasks in upstream workspaces (e.g. `^build`). Combined with content-addressed caching, this turns repeated CI runs into cache hits and keeps the monorepo fast as it grows.

tour.title: Environment and Shared Infrastructure
tour.description: All cross-cutting configuration enters through `packages/infra/src/env.ts`, which uses Zod to validate the DATABASE_URL, Better Auth secrets, email (Resend) credentials, platform-admin overrides, and frontend URLs. This single source of truth is consumed by both the API process and the shared infra package, so every later step (database, auth, agents) ultimately reads from here. The `.env.example` file shows newcomers exactly which variables they must set locally.
tour.languageLesson: Validating env vars with a Zod schema turns runtime configuration into a typed value. If a required variable is missing the process fails fast at startup with a clear error, instead of crashing later when an undefined string sneaks into a database URL or JWT secret.

tour.title: Local Postgres + pgvector
tour.description: Local development depends on Postgres 16 with the pgvector extension, provisioned via the Docker Compose service in `packages/infra/docker/compose.yaml`. The container exposes port 5490 -> 5432 and reads the same `.env` validated in Step 3. pgvector is not optional here — the Knowledge Base feature (Step 9) stores embeddings in this database and queries them with cosine similarity, so the choice of image is load-bearing.
tour.languageLesson: docker-compose service files declare images, port mappings, and volume mounts declaratively. Using `env_file` to source values from the repo `.env` keeps secrets out of the YAML and lets the same container definition work across machines without edits.

tour.title: Database Schema and Domain Model
tour.description: The Drizzle ORM schema is the canonical definition of TACO-IDE's data model. `auth.ts` mirrors Better Auth's user/session/organization/member/invitation tables, while `app.ts` defines the domain: classrooms, challenges, teaching assistants, work sessions, knowledge bases (with pgvector columns), conversation replays, and evaluations. The `schema/index.ts` barrel re-exports everything, and `docs/schema.sql` plus the initial Drizzle migration document the same shape as raw SQL for review and onboarding.
tour.languageLesson: Drizzle defines tables as TypeScript objects, so column types, foreign keys, and indexes all participate in type inference. `db.select().from(challenges)` returns a row type derived from the schema, giving you compile-time safety without a separate codegen step. SQL migrations stay alongside the schema and should be applied in numbered order — never rewritten after being shipped.

tour.title: Drizzle Client and Better Auth Setup
tour.description: With the schema in place, two singletons make it usable. `db/index.ts` instantiates a postgres-js connection and binds Drizzle to the schema barrel from Step 5, producing the `db` exported throughout the API. `auth/index.ts` configures Better Auth with the Drizzle adapter, the organization and admin plugins, the email senders for invitations and password reset, and password hashing. Together they form the foundation that every authenticated route relies on.

tour.title: API Process Entry Point
tour.description: `apps/api/src/index.ts` is the actual process entrypoint: it calls into `http/server.ts` to construct a Fastify app — wiring CORS, Swagger/OpenAPI documentation, Zod validation, and the v1 route tree — then listens on the configured port and installs SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers for graceful shutdown. This is where the Drizzle client and Better Auth instance from Step 6 get composed into a runnable HTTP service.

tour.title: Route Tree, Auth, and Authorization
tour.description: `routes/v1/index.ts` mounts every feature plugin — auth, challenges, chat, classrooms, knowledge-bases, organizations, status, users, work-sessions — under the `/v1` prefix. Two preHandler middlewares enforce security on top: `middlewares/auth.ts` resolves a Better Auth session into a loaded user plus active-organization membership, and `middlewares/authorization.ts` (the most depended-on backend module at fan-in 29) layers platform-admin, role-minimum, and permission-based checks on top. Every protected route in the codebase composes these two.
tour.languageLesson: Fastify preHandler hooks run after request parsing but before the route handler, making them the right place for auth and ACL checks. Attaching the loaded user to `request` lets every downstream handler stay typed against a non-null user without re-querying the database.

tour.title: Knowledge Base Pipeline
tour.description: Knowledge Base is the project's signature feature: teachers upload documents that become semantically searchable context for the AI tutor. The ingestion pipeline lives in `apps/api/src/services/`: `document-parser.ts` extracts text (pdf-parse for PDFs, Pandoc for everything else), `chunking.ts` splits by markdown hierarchy with overlap, `embedding.ts` calls an OpenAI- or Voyage-style API to vectorize each chunk, `file-storage.ts` persists the original under `uploads/documents/{orgId}/{kbId}/`, and `knowledge-base-search.ts` runs pgvector cosine-similarity queries against the resulting `knowledge_base_chunk` rows.
tour.languageLesson: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) splits a corpus into chunks, embeds each chunk as a vector, and stores the vectors next to the text. At query time the user's question is embedded with the same model and a nearest-neighbour search (here, pgvector cosine similarity) returns the top-k chunks to feed the LLM as context.

tour.title: LangGraph AI Agents
tour.description: TACO-IDE ships two LangGraph ReAct agents. The Teaching Assistant (`agents/teaching-assistant/agent.ts`) is the student-facing tutor with tools for executing Python code and retrieving knowledge-base context from Step 9. The Teacher's Companion (`agents/teachers-companion/agent.ts`) helps educators draft and refine challenges. Both share `llm-factory.ts`, which builds a validated ChatOpenAI-compatible client and exposes `AgentTimeoutError` so chat routes can enforce request budgets, and `sse-events.ts`, which formats responses for Server-Sent Events streaming to the browser.
tour.languageLesson: ReAct (Reason + Act) agents alternate between LLM-generated reasoning steps and tool calls until the model emits a final answer. LangGraph models this as a stateful graph of nodes, which makes it natural to stream intermediate tokens and tool results back over SSE so the UI can show progress as the agent thinks.

tour.title: Typed Client Generation with Kubb
tour.description: The bridge between backend and frontend is Kubb. `apps/api/kubb.config.ts` reads the Fastify-generated `swagger.yaml` and emits TypeScript types into `@repo/types`, Zod schemas, and React Query hooks straight into `apps/web/src/kubb/hooks/`. Whenever a route's Zod schema changes, running `npm run kubb` regenerates fully typed clients — the frontend never hand-writes API request types, which is what keeps the contract honest across the two apps.
tour.languageLesson: OpenAPI codegen turns a server-side schema into client-side types and hooks. Pairing it with React Query gives you cache-aware data fetching for free: each generated hook knows its query key, response type, and invalidation surface, so the frontend stays in lockstep with the backend without manual typing.

tour.title: Next.js Frontend Shell
tour.description: On the web side, `app/layout.tsx` is the App Router root: it loads global CSS, sets metadata, and wraps the tree in the React Query provider that Kubb hooks (Step 11) depend on. `middleware.ts` runs at the edge to check the Better Auth session cookie and redirect unauthenticated visitors to the login page, and `(inside)/layout.tsx` is the authenticated shell that adds the navbar, footer, and a no-active-organization fallback. `UserContext.tsx` (fan-in 17) exposes the current user, role helpers, organization auto-selection, and logout to the whole tree.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js App Router nests layouts: a route inherits every layout from its segments. Edge middleware runs before any layout renders, which makes it the right place for auth gating — a redirect there avoids shipping a flash of unauthenticated UI to the client.

tour.title: Frontend Data Access and Problem Workspace
tour.description: `lib/apiClient.ts` is the HTTP client that every Kubb-generated hook delegates to: it builds query strings, serializes JSON, surfaces a typed `ApiError`, and on 401 signs the user out and redirects to login — the mirror of Step 8's server-side auth. The student experience lives in `app/problem/[id]/page.tsx`, which composes the challenge view, and `store/useCodeEditorStore.ts` (Zustand) holds the Monaco editor instance, code, stdin, and execution output, including running Python in the browser via Pyodide.
tour.languageLesson: Zustand stores are plain functions returning state plus actions, with no provider boilerplate. Selecting a slice with `useStore(s => s.code)` re-renders only when that slice changes, which is what keeps a code editor performant even as the user types every keystroke into the store.

tour.title: CI/CD Deployment
tour.description: The capstone: the GitHub Actions workflow `main_portal-taco-ai.yml` builds the Next.js web app and deploys it to the Azure Web App `portal-taco-ai` on every push to `main`. This is the last link in the chain — README to monorepo to database to API to agents to frontend, and finally to production — so you can now trace any feature from a teacher's click in the browser back through every layer you've seen.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows declare triggers under `on:` (e.g. `push: branches: [main]`), parallelizable `jobs:`, and sequential `steps:`. Caching `~/.npm` and the Next.js `.next/cache` directory dramatically shortens build times because dependency installation and incremental compilation become cache hits across runs.
